counting_rules: Charge each original logical run/input path once; same path plus same SHA in local/archive wrappers adds no attempt. Different run paths remain separate even with identical bytes.
Reuse v1 primary1559input/15244case and44native ledger. The five v1tailinputs/44cases are among the new original inputs here and charged exactly once.
Reject same-path SHA drift; do not reinterpret an overwritten run as new evidence or silently omit it.

All input cases cost attempts, including failures, zero-frame rejection, held/full reruns, counters and fixtures. Missing output at cutoff still costs every input case. Summary pass counts are never a budget denominator.
Only files stable and timestamped at/before fixed cutoff are accepted. After-cutoff or unstable outputs are not retroactively passed. No future calls are covered.

Native Godot write-movie command artifacts use the complete normalized command identity and original artifact provenance, merging only copies as in v1; each new recording command costs one. FFmpeg/segment copies cost zero Godot calls.

new_archive_wrapper.policy: Same original logical input path plus same SHA is one attempt lineage; ZIP object deduplication/repackaging adds zero physics cost.

limitations: This is a fixed artifact cutoff, not a live or future balance and not budget authorization. N12/N13 authoring may create inputs after cutoff.
Prior13archives and baseline outputs inherit the hash-bound v1 verification; this increment does not reparse their full payloads. Only new v9 parts/whole/index and new original run results are read.
Unpersisted or overwritten terminal invocations and other worktrees remain UNKNOWN; a filesystem ledger cannot prove their absence.
No human fun/production approval and no new physical success are inferred from cost.

recompute.method: Read-only incremental program embedded for audit; source sets a new current cutoff on each execution and requires nonexistent output filenames. To reproduce this exact snapshot use cutoff_unix above and alternate outputs.
